Fixes https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/issues/15862.

As an aside, float-specific functions on non-floats also currently don't preserve NULLs:

<details>
<summary>Non-float</summary>

```python
import polars as pl

df = pl.Series("a", [1, None]).to_frame()

v = df.with_columns(
    **{
        x: getattr(pl.col("a"), x)().alias(x)
        for x in ["is_nan", "is_not_nan", "is_finite", "is_infinite"]
    }
)

print(v)

shape: (2, 5)
┌──────┬────────┬────────────┬───────────┬─────────────┐
│ a    ┆ is_nan ┆ is_not_nan ┆ is_finite ┆ is_infinite │
│ ---  ┆ ---    ┆ ---        ┆ ---       ┆ ---         │
│ i64  ┆ bool   ┆ bool       ┆ bool      ┆ bool        │
╞══════╪════════╪════════════╪═══════════╪═════════════╡
│ 1    ┆ false  ┆ true       ┆ true      ┆ false       │
│ null ┆ false  ┆ true       ┆ true      ┆ false       │
└──────┴────────┴────────────┴───────────┴─────────────┘

```

</details>

issue_context.title: Asymmetry between `is_nan` and `is_not_nan`
issue_context.body:
### Checks

- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.
- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.

### Reproducible example

```python
import polars as pl

ldf = pl.DataFrame({"a": [1.0, None, float("nan")]}).lazy()
ldf.select(pl.col("a").is_nan()).collect()
# [False, NULL, True]
ldf.select(pl.col("a").is_not_nan()).collect()
# [True, True, False]
```


### Log output

```shell
run ProjectionExec
run ProjectionExec
```


### Issue description

Where `is_nan` maintains missing values, `is_not_nan` does not: a `null` value returns `true` to the question `is_not_nan`.

This breaks the identity one might expect that `col.is_nan().not_() == col.is_not_nan()`. Is this asymmetry deliberate?

### Expected behavior

I was expecting `is_not_nan` to be the negation of `is_nan`, preserving null values.

I note that this appears to have been a deliberate change in https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/pull/4119 as a result of fixing #4101.

comments: I think that's by accident. Should be symmetric indeed.

The natural change which just preserves the validity mask unfortunately has follow-on consequences. For example, it changes the behaviour of `fill_nan`. The reason is that `pl.when` treats `null` as `False` in a `pl.when().then().otherwise()` expression and `col.fill_nan(value)` is implemented as `pl.when(col.is_not_nan()).then(col).otherwise(value)`. So I guess to fix this one needs to decide on the semantics of `when` in the presence of nulls.
IMO the user must adapt the predicate for that.
The user in this case is `fill_nan`. I'll try pull at the loose thread in a few days and see how much of the jumper is left...

> IMO the user must adapt the predicate for that.

Meaning that `when` will pass-through null values now? Will `filter` as well?

> Meaning that `when` will pass-through null values now? Will `filter` as well?

No, `when` doesn't change. You must ensure your predicate (the mask you pass) reflects the null behavior you'd like to see.

review_comments: This PR can be considered a fix since it didn't conform to polars' NULL-semantics, but since existing users would need to update their queries like this, it can also be considered as a breaking change.
Yes, it is a fix. Sometimes they are unlucky. :/
I think we can save a `negate + allocation` if we say `& ca.is_not_null()`. In that case we can use the validity mask directly and convert that to boolean array.
